chunks: He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, reported to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Yasir, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha, Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon them both, who said:
When the rulers utter lies, the rain is withheld. And when the monarch is oppressive, the state is weakened. And when zakat is withheld, the livestock perish.

key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam
key_terms.السلطان: The monarch, sovereign, or supreme political authority
key_terms.المواشي: Livestock, cattle — the economic backbone of early Islamic society
key_terms.الولاة: Rulers, governors — those entrusted with public authority

ai.seo_question: What are the consequences of rulers lying, tyranny, and withholding zakat according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) describes three societal sins and their cosmic consequences: rulers lying causes drought, tyrannical authority leads to the decline of the state, and withholding zakat results in livestock death. This teaching, delivered in the context of the Abbasid era when political corruption was rampant, connects the moral conduct of leaders and citizens to divine blessings in the natural world.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Yasir, from Abdul Hasan al-Ridha, ‘Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon him, who said:

"When the rulers utter lies, the rains are withheld. And when the monarch is oppressive, the country is weakened and when Zakat is withheld, the livestock (upon which Zakat has been due) suffer death."
